RESUME (P1.1) — CORRECT. trace.ts:159 `hydratedPayload` reads `join(runDir, call.payload_path)`, JSON.parses it, caches into `payloads[index]`, sets `hydrated[index]=true` BEFORE the read (so a missing/unparseable file is cached as `undefined`, never retried), and the try/catch + `existsSync` guard skip gracefully instead of throwing. `record()` pushes `hydrated=true` (trace.ts:202), so a fresh run's in-memory payloads are returned with zero file reads — hydration only fires for restored (resume) calls. File I/O stays inside the recorder; feed-refs.ts imports no `fs` and only calls `recordedCalls()`. `buildFeedRefsUniverse` then resolves the restored chunk_refs/article_refs/text via the shared `collectRefsFromCalls`. Verified by the disk-round-trip, missing-payload, and hydrate-once tests.

WARM CACHE (P1.2) — CORRECT. Fragment computed at WRITE via `buildFeedRefsFragmentForAgent` (retrieve.ts:529), stored in new `refs_universe_json` column. On HIT the fragment is pushed to `services.feedRefsCacheFragments` (retrieve.ts:454) and unioned by `buildFeedRefsUniverse` (feed-refs.ts:99-103). Both `citations_resolve` (citation-lint.ts:127) and `feed_facts_quotes_verbatim` (linting.ts:311) read from the single `FEED_REFS_UPSTREAM_KEY` universe, so both pass without any synthetic call. NULL/legacy fragment is a hard MISS (retrieve-cache.ts:88 `if (row.refs_universe_json === null) return null`) — not injected — so it can't poison lint; validate-on-lookup is NOT the sole mechanism. Fragment extraction reuses `collectRefsFromCalls`, so no divergent second implementation.

NO TRACE POLLUTION — CONFIRMED. Fragment rides an in-memory array only; nothing writes to the recorder or feed-trace.json on a hit.

MIGRATION — CORRECT for the in-scope (cold-start pipeline-owned) DB: version 4 > current max 3, nullable ALTER, pre-existing rows get NULL and behave as a miss (never crash prepare()). runMigrations applies by `MAX(_schema_migrations.version)`.

Findings:
- P2 (inherited, escalated) store-migrations.ts:117 / retrieve-cache.ts:66. On a LEGACY dossier-era memory.db (`_schema_migrations` max ~23), migration 4 is skipped so `refs_universe_json` is never added, and C9's new `SELECT ... refs_universe_json` throws "no such column" at `prepare()` → run crashes. This sharpens the implementer's own documented P2#7 from "relies on final shape" to an actual init crash, because C9 is the first code to reference the new column. Fix: reuse the same DB the cutover cold-starts, or guard the column via a `PRAGMA table_info` check. Out of C9's stated scope (cold-start assumption) but should be tracked.

REGRESSIONS: none. Cache keys/fingerprints unchanged; trace contract unchanged; fresh-run happy path unchanged (empty fragment array unions to nothing). typecheck `npx tsc --project tsconfig.typecheck.json` exit 0. Implementer reported full suite 180 files / 1543 tests pass, 0 fail (C8 gate); the two C9 files run green here (23/23).

Test quality: strong, non-hollow — resume hydration is a real disk round-trip across two recorder instances, hydrate-once mutates the file after first read, null-fragment-miss is mutation-documented, and the warm-cache test asserts no LLM re-dispatch plus universe resolution end-to-end.
